reframe.title: Fernley's task is to get young adults in Ireland to know and try a drink they may not yet know how to place.
reframe.line: Awareness and trial for a Cork sparkling iced tea, spring to summer 2027, with no research yet behind the audience view.

claims.text: The client asks for two things: be known among the audience, and be tried.
The audience is 18 to 34 year olds in Ireland.
Fernley is a Cork-based sparkling iced tea brand.
We believe trial depends on people being able to picture the taste first. This is a hypothesis to confirm.

gap_chart.title: We cannot chart Fernley's awareness or trial gap yet because no market figures were supplied.
gap_chart.takeaway: Before the pitch we need awareness, trial and category figures from the client or from research.

barrier.title: The likely barrier to trial is uncertainty about what the drink is, not dislike of it. This must be tested.

points.text: The brief says nothing yet about how the audience sees iced tea. That is a research question, not a known fact.
A new drink that is hard to place may be hard to picture tasting. This is a hypothesis to confirm.
The client wants trial, so the work must lower the risk of a first sip.

insight_candidates.observation: Hypothesis to confirm: at the chiller, young adults in Ireland may not be able to tell whether a sparkling iced tea is a tea or a soft drink.
insight_candidates.tension: They may be open to something new, yet a drink they cannot place is one they cannot picture tasting.
insight_candidates.implication: So Fernley should show what sparkling iced tea tastes like before it asks anyone to pick up a can.
insight_candidates.not_in_brief: Names a possible barrier: confusion between the tea and soft-drink categories. The brief names no barrier.
insight_candidates.from: No finding or verbatim was supplied. This grows only from the product description and the trial objective. It is an untested hypothesis.
insight_candidates.swap_test: Passes narrowly. It depends on sparkling iced tea sitting between two categories, so a cola could not say it. Another hybrid drink could.
insight_candidates.confidence: low: hypothesis only, needs shopper research

insight_candidates.observation: Hypothesis to confirm: young adults in Ireland may see tea as something they grew up with at home, not something they would choose on a summer day out.
insight_candidates.tension: They may feel at home with tea, yet never think of it when they want something cold and fizzy.
insight_candidates.implication: So Fernley, a Cork tea brand, should take tea from the kitchen table out into the Irish summer, cold and sparkling.
insight_candidates.not_in_brief: Suggests the audience already knows tea but not this occasion. If true, awareness means a new moment for tea, not a new drink.
insight_candidates.from: No verbatim or finding was supplied. This grows from the brand being tea and the campaign running in spring and summer. It is an untested hypothesis.
insight_candidates.swap_test: Passes. Only a tea brand can turn familiarity with tea into a reason to try. A cola, water or juice brand could not say it.
insight_candidates.confidence: low: hypothesis only, needs qualitative interviews with the audience

insight_candidates.observation: Hypothesis to confirm: young adults may expect iced tea to be sweet and still, and the word sparkling may not yet change that expectation.
insight_candidates.tension: They may want a cold drink with character, yet assume iced tea is a sugary drink with a tea label.
insight_candidates.implication: So Fernley should lead with the sparkle and the tea together, not rely on the words iced tea alone.
insight_candidates.not_in_brief: Suggests the category name itself may hold back trial. The brief gives no view of the category.
insight_candidates.from: No category research was supplied. This grows only from the product being sparkling iced tea. It is an untested hypothesis.
insight_candidates.swap_test: Passes. It depends on the iced tea category's reputation, so a rival from another category could not say it.
insight_candidates.confidence: low: hypothesis only, needs category perception research

insight.why: It is the only candidate that just a tea brand could own, and the cheapest to test early. All three are unproven until research is supplied.
insight.title: Young adults may know tea well but not think of it for summer, so Fernley can make tea the cold, sparkling choice. This must be confirmed.

evidence.text: Fernley is a Cork-based sparkling iced tea brand.
The campaign runs from spring to summer 2027 in Ireland.
The client wants 18 to 34 year olds to know Fernley and try it.
No audience research was supplied, so this insight is a hypothesis to confirm.

audience.title: We are talking to 18 to 34 year olds in Ireland, and we do not yet know how they see tea.
audience.two_halves: Not defined in the inputs. Proposed for research: people who drink tea at home and people who do not.

persona.name: Aoife
persona.line: Drinks tea at home every day, but has never thought of reaching for one cold in the sun.

objection.text: This insight rests on no research. Why should we believe it?
objection.answer: We should not believe it yet. It is a testable hypothesis, and we propose quick audience interviews to confirm or replace it before creative development.

from_to.from: Tea is something young adults may know only from home. This is a hypothesis.
from_to.to: Fernley makes tea something to try cold and sparkling this summer.

rtbs.text: It is a sparkling iced tea, which is tea made cold and fizzy.
It comes from Fernley Drinks, a Cork-based brand.
Further reasons to believe must come from the client. None were supplied.

reasons: IC1: Swap in "[client]" and "[category]": "when choosing a cold drink quickly, young adults reach for the brand they already know rather than an unfamiliar can" is true of any drink brand.; Nothing ties it to Fernley or sparkling iced tea; any rival drink brand could say "an unfamiliar can" loses to the known brand.; It cites prompt:1, which gives only the objective, and req:R2, which has no text. The source note says "No finding was supplied", so the habit claim goes beyond the evidence.

IC2: "a more grown-up alternative to the usual fizzy drinks, but keep buying the usual ones" could be said by any non-cola or better-for-you drink; swap in "[client]" and it still reads true.; It never mentions tea, sparkle or Cork. Any rival alternative drink could claim "an upgrade they can enjoy, not a compromise".; brief:audience and brief:background give only the age range and a description of the brand. Nothing says young adults want a grown-up alternative to fizzy drinks, and the source note admits "No verbatim or finding was supplied."

IC3: brief:background says only that Fernley is a Cork sparkling iced tea brand; prompt:1 gives the objective. Neither says how young adults see iced tea, and the source note admits "No category research was supplied."
